name: The Mitsui Kyoto, a Luxury Collection Hotel & Spa
positioning: HOTEL THE MITSUI KYOTO, a Luxury Collection Hotel & Spa: a central Kyoto hotel beside Nijo Castle on the former Mitsui family estate, with a courtyard garden and hot spring baths fed from below the property
best_for: Travelers who want a central Kyoto base a short walk from Nijo Castle
Guests who want hot spring bathing, from a thermal spring to a suite with its own outdoor onsen bath
Travelers interested in Kyoto history, garden design and the tea ceremony

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Kyoto, adjacent to Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Nijo Castle is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
The hotel is built on a 250-year-old historic site that was once the home of the executive branch of the Mitsui family.
Guests arrive through an ornate wooden gateway that once marked the entrance to the Mitsui clan's Kyoto residence.
Guest rooms are a modern reimagining of the traditional Japanese tearoom, with carefully chosen natural materials elevated using artisanal skills.
The interiors are by designer Andre Fu.
Room bathtubs are fashioned out of stone and are generously sized.
Spa treatments draw on the principles of Japanese Anma massage, blended with facial treatments from abroad.
Restoration specialists Yasui Mokuzoku recreated the SHIKI-NO-MA to reflect the Okushoin, the room at the heart of the original Mitsui residence.
Ambassadors trained by a Mushakouji Senke tea master perform a seated tea procedure at CHAKYO.
The signature restaurant TOKI serves French cuisine and is led by Chef Tetsuya Asano.
The hotel has been awarded Three MICHELIN Keys.

highlights.text: The Thermal Spring is sourced from a natural hot spring about 1,000 meters directly below the hotel.
The central courtyard garden, designed by landscape architect Shunsaku Miyagi, is a modern recreation of the garden of the former Mitsui residence.
The Onsen Suite features an outdoor bath fed by natural hot springs.
The Nijo Suite offers panoramic views of Nijo Castle.
The hotel offers a private tour of Kiyomizu-dera Temple, where resident monks guide guests into sacred spaces normally closed to the public.

considerations.text: The minimum age to check in is 18.
Guests wear swimsuits to bathe in the Thermal Spring.
Conde Nast Traveler describes a very grown-up atmosphere at the hotel.
